newsitem.title: AFGHANISTAN: NGOs do less in Kabul until clear if women can work.
newsitem.headline: NGOs do less in Kabul until clear if women can work.

text.p: A number of non-governmental aid agencies have reduced their programmes in Kabul until the position of their female employees has benn clarified, a spokesman for the aid community said on Sunday.

"Some non-governmental organisations (NGOs) have reduced their programmes until they can get formal authorisation from the authorities." Ross Everson of the Agency Coordinating Body for Afghanistan told Reuters.
"We have a security problem with women aid workers. We have the ministers saying one thing and the Taleban militia doing the opposite." he said.
"We need the authorities to publicly support the NGOs, and particularly their women's programmes. Until they do that we are always running the risk of security problems." he said.
The Taleban have said that Afghan women are allowed to work in the medical sector, but, according to Everson, the Taleban are still preventing women from going to work.
The Taleban, a militant Islamic and mainly Pushtun-speaking militia, have overrun much of southern Afghanistan and are trying to impose a strict fundamentalist order.
